extracted.intended_audience: fiction authors who have written (or plan to write) transgender characters and are seeking sensitivity reading or guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for fiction writers on how sensitivity readers evaluate transgender characters and what authors should expect and do to produce respectful, believable representation. Covers feedback format, common pitfalls, narrative balance, and author mindset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced feedback: highlight strengths and note missteps
rubrics_metrics.description: The sensitivity reader marks both what works and what doesn't: "I mark down the cool sentences, the nice language tricks, and the descriptions that make my heart tremble. But I also mark down your missteps..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect positive highlights (memorable lines, effective description) alongside critical notes. Examples of missteps to look for include unnecessary references to binders or underwear, an abundance of mirrors, or inner monologues that run "too far, for too long." Feedback is intended to be constructive, not punitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-document feedback format
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback is delivered in two parts: a separate impressions/book-report document and inline manuscript comments: "I open two documents: one to write down impressions and do a simple book report, and the other one is your manuscript, where I will write comments next to the text..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first document contains background/contextual notes (misconceptions, what you did well, what could be better). The second contains line-by-line or paragraph-level comments in the manuscript (often many colored comments). Expect possibly a multi-page PDF plus heavily annotated manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify common misconceptions and explain why
rubrics_metrics.description: The sensitivity reader will "add background information: what are common misconceptions and why, and which ones are present in your work."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should expect explanations of cultural or factual misunderstandings, not just corrections. The reader will point out which misconceptions appear in the text and provide reasons/context so the author can learn and avoid repeating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call out stereotypes and overused tropes
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitivity readers identify stereotypical or overdone elements in characterization and background: e.g., "the bullying in the background is an easy stereotype, and has sometimes been overdone..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes will flag clichés (bullying-as-background, trauma tropes, single-story arcs) and advise whether they are appropriate given the piece's genre and tone. Guidance may include suggesting reduction, replacement, or recontextualization of the trope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative balance: adjust focus on trans identity vs other plot elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers may recommend rebalancing the narrative if the trans identity is overemphasized: "my suggestion may be to change a whole arc... because the focus on trans identity could use lightening up... if being trans is just a part of who your written character is, it'd be cooler to read about this whole other thing happening (that is, the plot)"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice can range from small edits to substantial arc changes (potentially large word-count revisions). The goal is to integrate identity as one facet of a character rather than making it the only plot driver, unless the story's central theme requires that focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete detail sensitivity: watch for clichéd physical/behavioral markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain recurring details tend to signal stereotyping and are called out specifically: "the way you mention binders or underwear; the abundance of mirrors; the inner monologues..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should scrutinize specific props, scenes, or internalization that become shorthand for identity. Readers will point to these concrete instances and recommend alternatives or reductions to avoid flattening a character into tropes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach and tone of feedback: empathy, conversation, not a lecture
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitivity reading is framed as helping inform author empathy rather than lecturing: "I try to put into words what can only be lived, and to do so in a way that helps inform author empathy... It’s not a lecture, but a conversation; and no single sensitivity reader has all the answers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should expect collaborative, empathetic commentary rather than prescriptive policing. Readers acknowledge limits to their own knowledge and may present suggestions as conversation starters rather than absolute rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and community consultation underpin feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers support their notes by consulting resources and lived experience: "We check resources, re-read books we have full of notes, and talk with some of our close friends (also trans). It is not an exact science."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback is informed by a mix of reference material and community insight. Authors can expect citations, recommended reads, or explanations grounded in lived experience; however, some judgments remain subjective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author mindset and process recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance to authors about how to approach receiving feedback: breathe; write with care; talk to friends; listen; don't take feedback personally; sensitivity reading is not a test; use what you learn; don't give up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific bullet advice from the post: "Breathe." "Write with care, because we want to avoid intention harm, but don’t fear writing!" "Talk to your friends, meet people outside your bubble or comfort zone, and listen." "Don’t take our feedback, notes, and marks personally... A sensitivity read is about what you can learn from us. It is not a test you need to pass..." Use feedback constructively to improve representation and keep writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: High standard of care: treat characters as if they were the reader's own
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitivity readers aim to help authors by treating characters "as carefully as if they were our own." The service is rooted in care and the desire to improve work so it resonates ethically and emotionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect attentive, invested critiques intended to make characters more authentic and to increase emotional impact. The post promises that using sensitivity feedback will make the book stronger and more memorable to readers.
